raw_segments.text: Blanche and Mary were of equal stature, straight and tall as poplars.
Mary was too slim for her height, but Blanche was molded like a diane.
I regarded her, of course, with special interest.
First, I wished to see whether her appearance accorded with Mrs. Fairfax's description.
Secondly, whether it at all resembled the fancy miniature I had painted of her, and
thirdly, it will out, whether it were such as I should fancy likely to suit Mr. Rochester's
